name: arc-3x3-block-encoding
description: Use when a 12x12 ARC grid appears to encode a 4x4 output in 3x3 blocks.
---

# Decode a 3×3 block-encoded ARC grid

Use this when demonstrations map a 12×12 input to a 4×4 output and the input appears divided into uniform or nearly uniform 3×3 patches.

1. Divide the input into 4 rows × 4 columns of non-overlapping 3×3 blocks.
2. Determine the background color from the demo (in the observed task it is 5).
3. For each block, ignore background cells and emit the remaining foreground color as the corresponding output cell. Blocks may contain several background cells; foreground cells encode the pixel.
4. Assemble the 16 decoded colors in the same top-to-bottom, left-to-right block order.
5. Before submitting, verify the rule against every supplied demo and check that each block has a consistent foreground color. If a block has multiple foreground colors, do not force this rule; request another demo or reconsider the encoding.

Observed example: a 12×12 grid with background 5 decoded into a 4×4 grid by reading the unique non-5 color in each 3×3 block. This was validated against one demo and a test instance.",
